chunks: And Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated from Ibn Sayabah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
A man asked him and said to him: “May I be your ransom, I hear some people saying that agriculture is disliked.”

So he said: “Cultivate and plant. No, by Allah, people have done no work more halal and better than it. By Allah, they will surely continue to cultivate crops and date palms after the خروج of the Dajjal.”

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: more lawful and more clearly halal
key_terms.ازْرَعُوا: cultivate; a command to sow crops
key_terms.الدَّجَّالِ: the Dajjal, mentioned here in an eschatological context
key_terms.الزِّرَاعَةَ: agriculture or farming as a form of livelihood
key_terms.النَّخْلَ: date palms, a key cultivated tree

ai.seo_question: Is farming considered disliked in Islam, or is it a praiseworthy and halal livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the claim that agriculture is makruh and instead praises farming and planting as among the most halal and wholesome forms of work. It also indicates the enduring importance of cultivation, mentioning that people will continue sowing crops and date palms even after the emergence of the Dajjal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3907 - Muhammad bin Khalid narrated from Ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (as):
A man asked Imam (as): "May I be your ransom! I hear some people saying that farming is disliked."

Imam (as) said: "Cultivate and plant! By Allah (swt), people have not engaged in any work more lawful and pure than this.
By Allah (swt), they will continue to cultivate crops and date palms even after the emergence of the Dajjal."
